title: Thanthai Periyar and the Live Electric Wire: Rationalism at the Public Square
summary: At an open-air rally, when an orthodox opponent interrupted asserting that ancient rituals possess mystical immunity, Periyar challenged him with disarming humor: 'Come touch this live generator cable while chanting your mantras; if nature spares you, I will become your disciple!'
keywords: Thanthai Periyar and the Live Electric Wire: Rationalism at the Public Square
full_text:
In 1948, under the open skies of Erode, thousands had gathered to listen to Thanthai Periyar E.V. Ramasamy. With his long flowing white beard and walking stick, Periyar sat on a wooden chair, speaking in the earthy, colloquial language of the Tamil countryside.

During the question-and-answer session, an orthodox critic stood up from the front row:
"Periyar! You constantly attack religious customs and ancient shastras. Our sacred traditions possess invisible spiritual powers that your secular science cannot fathom! How dare you call them useless?"

Periyar smiled broadly, running his hand through his beard. The crowd stirred, but Periyar gestured for complete quiet.

"Ayya, I welcome your courage," Periyar said warmly. "Let us not fight with words. Let us conduct a simple empirical test right here on this dais."

Periyar pointed to the thick black insulated cable running from the diesel generator to the stage floodlights.

"Inside that wire runs 230 volts of electric current," Periyar continued with twinkling eyes. "Electricity is pure material nature. It does not read Sanskrit; it does not care whether a man is a high-caste priest or an untouchable worker.

"Now, sir, you climb onto this stage. Recite your most potent mantras, sprinkle sacred water on your fingers, and grab that live copper wire. If your mystical verses insulate your body from the electric shock, I will publicly bow before you, tear up my books, and follow you as a devoted disciple! But if you refuse to touch it, you must admit that nature obeys the laws of science, not human superstitions!"

The entire audience erupted into thunderous laughter and applause. The orthodox gentleman quietly sat down, smiling sheepishly.

Periyar leaned forward:
"You see, friends? Deep down, even the most orthodox among us knows that science is real and mantras cannot stop a current. All I ask you to do is apply that exact same common sense to every social superstition that divides humanity!"
